--- id: synthesis.uniform-pair-channel-of-a-tower-condensate-is-a-goldstone-rotor kind: claim version: 1 title: 'Finite Goldstone bound: a pairing-type condensate''s uniform pair channel is a rotor' status: proved region: synthesis subject: quantum-fields tags: [symmetry-breaking, car-algebra, mass-generation, no-go] proposed_by: kind: ai session: 2026-11-08-composite-higgs ai_involved: 'yes' credit: - name: Leon Butler role: direction - name: Claude Opus 5.5 role: proposal and drafting source: run 2026-11-08-composite-higgs review: draft about: - obj.tower.tower derivations: - name: main uses: - tower.ladder-pairs-satisfy-car-vectors@4 - tower.structure-tower-c-norms@10 - field-theory.imported-tower-limit@3 - field-theory.how-close-tower-comes-ccr@4 - field-theory.composite-scalars-mean-field-level@5 - synthesis.tower-pairing-gap-at-fixed-charges-is-twice-the-quasiparticle-energy@2 proof: proof-main.tex checked_by: - kind: check ref: check.py::check_no_order_parameter_in_a_sector - kind: check ref: check.py::check_variational_bounds_on_every_sector - kind: check ref: check.py::check_single_shell_rotor_and_uniform_channel - kind: check ref: check.py::check_collective_limit_at_fixed_gap - kind: proof derivation: main lineage: motivated_by: - synthesis.rung-field-is-odd-in-the-tower-and-its-modes-carry-no-even-doublet - synthesis.exact-window-sugawara-identity-and-luttinger-normal-modes-of-tower-density-waves extraction: open_problem: op.qft-bosons-and-the-rung-field note: >- Adversarial attack on the problem's last two items (a gapped helicity-zero composite scalar from tower pairing, beyond mean field). Question: when a tower condensate breaks a continuous symmetry, is the uniform pair mode necessarily gapless, and with what finite-size splitting? Answer, exactly: (i) a charged field has no expectation in any sector vector, so a finite order parameter needs an eigenspace of H that meets two sectors; (ii) the variational bound on the sector ground energies by a charged field; (iii) for a pairing-type element H_0 - G X X* with [H_0, X] = eps X and [X, X*] a function of the charges, the second difference of the sector ground energies is at most G times the step of that function, whatever the size, and with the ground state in a sector on which neither X nor X* vanishes both neighbouring levels lie in [0, that bound]: a finite Goldstone (rotor) bound, a gaplessness statement only where G times the step of c tends to 0; (iv) on the stored single shell the bound is 2G and is attained, the ground state is the band state nearest gamma = (n_b + 1)/2 - K/G, and with a condensate the uniform channel P + P* has all its weight on the two neighbouring band levels, within 2G, the rotor over the stored pair-breaking threshold G n_b being at most 2/n_b (4E/n_b at fixed mean-field gap E); without a condensate the bound pair is gapped at 2K - G n_b and the gap closes exactly at the condensation threshold; the finite floor's ground state carries

!= 0 only at the degenerate couplings K/G = n_b/2 - n. Stored and cited, not refiled: the single-shell spectrum and the threshold G n_b = 2E (synthesis.tower-pairing-gap-at-fixed-charges-is-twice-the-quasiparticle-energy), the band and the condensation threshold G > 2K/n_b (field-theory.composite-scalars-mean-field-level), the quasi-spin ladder (field-theory.how-close-tower-comes-ccr), and the fact that the uniform channel P + P* moves only along the band and does not reach the threshold (synthesis.tower-pairing-gap-at-fixed-charges-is-twice-the-quasiparticle-energy (ii)); the adjoint v* = w is that of tower.structure-tower-c-norms. New here: the general clauses (i) to (iii), and in (iv) the global ground state, the rotor values and their bound, the explicit quasi-spin norms of the two neighbouring components, the symmetric-phase bound pair and the degenerate couplings. The doublet floor (two doublet modes and a singlet per block, uniform fields closing as u(3)) is not of the form (iii), since [P_a, P_b*] = delta_ab(n_b - N_s) - E_ba carries the isospin hopping; it is left to the constructive side, with one finding recorded in the run: in the condensed regime its ground state is not on the symmetric band (exact on the n_b = 2, 3 floors). Prior art, orientation only, cited from memory: the Goldstone theorem (Goldstone 1961; Goldstone, Salam and Weinberg 1962), Nambu's broken-symmetry pairing (Nambu 1960), the tower of states of a finite system with a broken continuous symmetry (Anderson 1952), the pairing-rotational band E(n) = G(n - gamma)^2 - G gamma^2 of nuclear physics, with a moment of inertia set by 1/G (Bes and Broglia, Nucl. Phys. 80 (1966) 289; Bohr and Mottelson, Nuclear Structure II), the quasi-spin solution of the degenerate pairing model (Kerman 1961, imported in synthesis.imported-quasi-spin-pairing-and-top-condensation, not used here). Ledger: transport-absent (finite CAR on tower planes; no transport completion used). --- ## formal Let the modes be tower planes, $a^{*} = v$, $a = w$, satisfying the canonical anticommutation relations (Theorem \claimref{tower.ladder-pairs-satisfy-car-vectors}, Fact \claimref{field-theory.imported-tower-limit}) on the Fock space $\mathcal{F}$, with its positive inner product and the adjoint $*$ ($v^{*} = w$, Theorem \claimref{tower.structure-tower-c-norms}). Let $Q_{1}, \dots, Q_{r}$ be commuting self-adjoint elements (charges) and $H$ a self-adjoint element commuting with each; a \emph{sector} is a nonzero joint eigenspace $\mathcal{F}_{s}$ ($Q_{i} = s_{i}$), and $E(s)$ is the lowest eigenvalue of $H$ on it. An element $X$ has charge $h \in \mathbb{R}^{r}$ if $[Q_{i}, X] = h_{i}X$ for all $i$; then $X\mathcal{F}_{s} \subset \mathcal{F}_{s+h}$ and $X^{*}$ has charge $-h$. \begin{enumerate} \item[(i)] \emph{(No order parameter in a sector.)} If $h \ne 0$, $\langle\psi, X\psi\rangle = 0$ for every $\psi$ in a sector. A one-dimensional eigenspace of $H$ lies in a sector; so an eigenvector $\psi$ of $H$ with $\langle\psi, X\psi\rangle \ne 0$ exists only if the eigenspace meets two sectors $s$ and $s + h$. \item[(ii)] \emph{(Variational bound.)} Let $\psi \in \mathcal{F}_{s}$, $H\psi = E(s)\psi$. If $X\psi \ne 0$, $E(s + h) - E(s) \le \langle X\psi, [H, X]\psi\rangle/\langle X\psi, X\psi\rangle$; if $X^{*}\psi \ne 0$, $E(s - h) - E(s) \le \langle X^{*}\psi, [H, X^{*}]\psi\rangle/\langle X^{*}\psi, X^{*}\psi\rangle$; each with equality exactly when $X\psi$ (respectively $X^{*}\psi$) is a lowest eigenvector of its sector. \item[(iii)] \emph{(Finite Goldstone bound for pairing-type elements.)} Let $H = H_{0} - GXX^{*}$, $G > 0$, $H_{0}$ self-adjoint commuting with the charges and $[H_{0}, X] = \varepsilon X$, $\varepsilon$ real, and let $C = [X, X^{*}]$ act on each sector as a scalar $c(s)$. Then the two quotients of (ii) are $\varepsilon + Gc(s)$ and $-\varepsilon - Gc(s - h)$, so whenever $X\psi \ne 0 \ne X^{*}\psi$, \[ E(s + h) + E(s - h) - 2E(s) \le G\bigl(c(s) - c(s - h)\bigr) , \] and if the ground state of $H$ lies in $\mathcal{F}_{s^{*}}$ with $X\psi \ne 0 \ne X^{*}\psi$, both $E(s^{*} \pm h) - E(s^{*})$ lie in $[0, G(c(s^{*}) - c(s^{*} - h))]$. \item[(iv)] \emph{(The single shell.)} For the stored element $H_{4} = \sum_{b}K(n_{a} + n_{c}) - GP^{*}P$, $P = \sum_{b}w_{a}w_{c}$, on $n_{b} \ge 2$ blocks, $K \ge 0$, $G > 0$ (Proposition \claimref{field-theory.composite-scalars-mean-field-level}(2)), with charges $N_{a}, N_{c}$ and $X = P^{*}$ ($h = (1, 1)$, $\varepsilon = 2K$, $C = N_{a} + N_{c} - n_{b}$), the bound of (iii) is $2G$ and is attained. The ground energy of $H_{4}$ is $\min_{n}E(n)$, $E(n) = 2Kn - Gn(n_{b} - n + 1) = G(n - \gamma)^{2} - G\gamma^{2}$, $\gamma = (n_{b} + 1)/2 - K/G$, attained at the band vector $\psi_{n^{*}} = (P^{*})^{n^{*}}\Omega$, $n^{*}$ an integer in $[0, n_{b} - 1]$ nearest $\gamma$ (and $0$ if $\gamma < \tfrac12$); the ground eigenspace is spanned by the $\psi_{n}$ with $E(n) = \min E$. \begin{enumerate} \item[(a)] \emph{(Condensed: $Gn_{b} > 2K$.)} $n^{*} \ge 1$, $E(n^{*} \pm 1) - E(n^{*}) = G(1 \pm 2(n^{*} - \gamma)) \in [0, 2G]$ with sum $2G$, and $(P + P^{*})\psi_{n^{*}} = \psi_{n^{*}+1} + n^{*}(n_{b} - n^{*} + 1)\psi_{n^{*}-1}$, $\|P^{*}\psi_{n^{*}}\|^{2} = (n^{*} + 1)(n_{b} - n^{*})\|\psi_{n^{*}}\|^{2}$, $\|P\psi_{n^{*}}\|^{2} = n^{*}(n_{b} - n^{*} + 1)\|\psi_{n^{*}}\|^{2}$: the uniform pair channel has all its weight on the two neighbouring band levels. Against the pair-breaking threshold $Gn_{b}$ at fixed numbers (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.tower-pairing-gap-at-fixed-charges-is-twice-the-quasiparticle-energy}(ii)) the larger of the two is at most $2/n_{b}$ of it, and at the gap equation $Gn_{b} = 2E$ it is at most $4E/n_{b}$, which tends to $0$ as $n_{b} \to \infty$ at fixed $E$ while the threshold stays $2E$. \item[(b)] \emph{(Symmetric: $Gn_{b} < 2K$.)} $\Omega$ is the unique ground state, and $P^{*}\Omega$ is an eigenvector at $2K - Gn_{b} > 0$, below the broken-pair level $2K$ of the same sector: the uniform pair is gapped, and its gap closes exactly at the condensation threshold $Gn_{b} = 2K$. \item[(c)] \emph{(Degenerate couplings.)} At $K/G = n_{b}/2 - n$, $n \in \{0, \dots, \lfloor n_{b}/2\rfloor\}$ (so that $K \ge 0$), $E(n) = E(n + 1) = \min E$ and $\psi = \psi_{n} + \psi_{n+1}$ is a ground state with $\langle\psi, P\psi\rangle = (n + 1)(n_{b} - n)\|\psi_{n}\|^{2} \ne 0$; at every other coupling every ground state of $H_{4}$ has $\langle P\rangle = 0$. \end{enumerate} \end{enumerate} Clauses (i) to (iv) are proved. \emph{Reading (argued).} With a condensate the uniform helicity-zero composite scalar of a floor is the Goldstone rotor of the broken pair phase, the finite-size form of the flat phase direction of Proposition \claimref{field-theory.composite-scalars-mean-field-level}(4): gapless in the collective limit at fixed mean-field gap, with no weight at the pair-breaking threshold. A gapped uniform composite exists only without a condensate. For a composite Higgs doublet, (i) applies to every charge the doublet carries, and the directions of its broken charges are of this rotor kind where (iii) applies; a gapped composite doublet would then have to be one that does not condense, or a mode outside the condensate's pair channel (such as a particle-number-conserving hopping doublet). The doublet floor and inter-condensate couplings, where $[X, X^{*}]$ is not a function of the charges, are not treated here. ## technical For pairing-type elements, whose pair commutator $[X, X^{*}]$ is a function of the charges: take tower modes on their Fock space, a set of commuting charges and a Hamiltonian commuting with them; sectors are the joint eigenspaces and $E(s)$ the lowest energy in sector $s$. (i) A field of nonzero charge has no expectation in any vector of one sector, so a finite system shows an order parameter only in an energy eigenspace that spans two sectors. (ii) Applying a charged field $X$ to a lowest vector of sector $s$ gives a trial vector for sector $s + h$, so $E(s + h) - E(s)$ is at most $\langle X\psi, [H, X]\psi\rangle/\|X\psi\|^{2}$, and likewise downwards with $X^{*}$. (iii) For $H = H_{0} - GXX^{*}$ with $[H_{0}, X] = \varepsilon X$ and $[X, X^{*}]$ equal to a function $c$ of the charges, the two quotients are $\varepsilon + Gc(s)$ and $-\varepsilon - Gc(s - h)$, so the second difference of the sector ground energies is at most $G(c(s) - c(s - h))$ at every size, and if the ground state's sector is one where $X$ and $X^{*}$ both act nontrivially both neighbouring sector energies are within that bound. (iv) For the stored single-shell pairing element, $c$ steps by $2$, so the bound is $2G$, and it is attained: the band $E(n) = G(n - \gamma)^{2} - G\gamma^{2}$ with $\gamma = (n_{b} + 1)/2 - K/G$ holds the ground state at the integer nearest $\gamma$. With a condensate ($Gn_{b} > 2K$) the two neighbouring band levels are within $2G$, they carry all of $(P + P^{*})\psi$, and against the pair-breaking threshold $Gn_{b} = 2E$ they are at most $2/n_{b}$ of it ($4E/n_{b}$ at fixed $E$). Without one ($Gn_{b} < 2K$) the vacuum is the unique ground state and the bound pair sits at $2K - Gn_{b}$, below the broken-pair level $2K$, closing at the condensation threshold. Only at the degenerate couplings $K/G = n_{b}/2 - n$ does a ground state carry $\langle P\rangle \ne 0$. The doublet floor and coupled condensates, where $[X, X^{*}]$ is not a function of the charges, are not covered. Reading (argued): for pairing-type elements a condensate's uniform composite scalar is its Goldstone rotor, and a gapped uniform composite needs no condensate; a gapped composite doublet would have to be a doublet that does not condense, or a mode outside the condensate's pair channel (such as a particle-number-conserving hopping doublet). ## lay When fermions pair up and the pairs condense, the condensate picks a phase, and changing that phase costs no energy in the idealised infinite system: the textbook Goldstone mode. This result asks what happens on a finite stack of the tower's modes, where everything is exact. The uniform pair mode then does not become a separate massive particle: all of its response sits on two neighbouring levels whose spacing shrinks in proportion to one over the number of pair sites, while the energy needed to break a pair stays fixed. In this model a genuinely gapped uniform pair state exists only when nothing condenses. The result covers this kind of pairing only: it does not cover a doublet of paired fermions on one stack, or two condensates coupled to each other, where the pairs' bookkeeping depends on more than the charges. As a reading (argued, on this model), a composite Higgs built from a condensate of this kind would not be the condensate's own uniform pair mode; it would have to be a mode outside that pair channel, or a doublet that does not condense. ## one-liner For a pairing-type tower element ([X, X*] a function of the charges) the sector ground energies have second difference at most G times the step of [X, X*]; on the single shell this is 2G, so a condensate's uniform pair channel is a rotor within 2G (at most 2/n_b of the pair-breaking threshold), and only without a condensate is the bound pair gapped, at 2K - G n_b.

proofs.proof-main.tex:
\emph{Preliminaries.} The modes are tower planes with $a^{*} = v$, $a = w$; by Theorem \claimref{tower.ladder-pairs-satisfy-car-vectors} and Fact \claimref{field-theory.imported-tower-limit} they satisfy the canonical anticommutation relations and act on the Fock space $\mathcal{F}$ with its positive inner product, for which $*$ is the adjoint; $v^{*} = w$ is the mutual adjointness of the ladder pairs in Theorem \claimref{tower.structure-tower-c-norms}. Everything below is finite-dimensional linear algebra on $\mathcal{F}$ with real coefficients; no unit is needed. Since the $Q_{i}$ are commuting self-adjoint operators, $\mathcal{F}$ is the orthogonal sum of the sectors $\mathcal{F}_{s}$, and since $H$ commutes with every $Q_{i}$ it maps each sector into itself, so $E(s)$, the lowest eigenvalue of $H$ on $\mathcal{F}_{s}$, is defined for every nonzero sector. If $X$ has charge $h$ then for $\psi \in \mathcal{F}_{s}$, $Q_{i}X\psi = XQ_{i}\psi + h_{i}X\psi = (s_{i} + h_{i})X\psi$, so $X\mathcal{F}_{s} \subset \mathcal{F}_{s+h}$; taking adjoints of $[Q_{i}, X] = h_{i}X$ gives $[Q_{i}, X^{*}] = -h_{i}X^{*}$, so $X^{*}$ has charge $-h$.

\emph{(i).} For $\psi \in \mathcal{F}_{s}$ and $h \ne 0$, $X\psi \in \mathcal{F}_{s+h}$, which is orthogonal to $\mathcal{F}_{s}$ (eigenspaces of a self-adjoint $Q_{i}$ with $h_{i} \ne 0$ for different eigenvalues), so $\langle\psi, X\psi\rangle = 0$. Each $Q_{i}$ commutes with $H$ and so maps each eigenspace of $H$ into itself; a one-dimensional eigenspace is then spanned by a common eigenvector of the $Q_{i}$, that is, it lies in a sector. More generally an eigenspace $V$ of $H$ is the orthogonal sum of its intersections $V_{s}$ with the sectors, and for $\psi = \sum_{s}\psi_{s}$ one has $\langle\psi, X\psi\rangle = \sum_{s}\langle\psi_{s+h}, X\psi_{s}\rangle$, which vanishes unless some $V_{s}$ and $V_{s+h}$ are both nonzero.

\emph{(ii).} Let $H\psi = E(s)\psi$, $\psi \in \mathcal{F}_{s}$, and $X\psi \ne 0$. Then $X\psi \in \mathcal{F}_{s+h}$ and $E(s+h)$ is at most its Rayleigh quotient, $E(s+h) \le \langle X\psi, HX\psi\rangle/\langle X\psi, X\psi\rangle$, with equality if and only if $X\psi$ is an eigenvector of $H$ for the eigenvalue $E(s+h)$ (finite dimension, $H$ self-adjoint on $\mathcal{F}_{s+h}$). Write $HX\psi = XH\psi + [H, X]\psi = E(s)X\psi + [H, X]\psi$; this gives the first bound. The second is the same argument for $X^{*}$, of charge $-h$.

\emph{(iii).} From $[H_{0}, X] = \varepsilon X$ with $\varepsilon$ real and $H_{0}$ self-adjoint, the adjoint gives $[H_{0}, X^{*}] = -\varepsilon X^{*}$. With $C = [X, X^{*}]$,
\[
[XX^{*}, X] = X[X^{*}, X] = -XC, \qquad [XX^{*}, X^{*}] = [X, X^{*}]X^{*} = CX^{*},
\]
so $[H, X] = \varepsilon X + GXC$ and $[H, X^{*}] = -\varepsilon X^{*} - GCX^{*}$. On $\psi \in \mathcal{F}_{s}$, $XC\psi = c(s)X\psi$, and $X^{*}\psi \in \mathcal{F}_{s-h}$ gives $CX^{*}\psi = c(s - h)X^{*}\psi$. Hence the two quotients of (ii) are exactly $\varepsilon + Gc(s)$ and $-\varepsilon - Gc(s - h)$, which are the two inequalities, and adding them bounds the second difference by $G(c(s) - c(s - h))$. If the ground state of $H$ lies in $\mathcal{F}_{s^{*}}$, then $E(s^{*}) \le E(s^{*} \pm h)$, so both differences are nonnegative, and their sum, hence each, is at most $G(c(s^{*}) - c(s^{*} - h))$.

\emph{(iv).} For $H_{4}$ take the charges $N_{a}$, $N_{c}$ and $X = P^{*} = \sum_{b}v_{c}v_{a}$, which raises each by one: $h = (1, 1)$. $H_{0} = \sum_{b}K(n_{a} + n_{c}) = KN$ with $N = N_{a} + N_{c}$ has $[N, P^{*}] = 2P^{*}$, so $\varepsilon = 2K$. By Proposition \claimref{field-theory.how-close-tower-comes-ccr}, $[P, P^{*}] = n_{b} - N$, so $C = [P^{*}, P] = N - n_{b}$, which on the sector $(N_{a}, N_{c})$ is the scalar $N_{a} + N_{c} - n_{b}$; on $(n, n)$, $c = 2n - n_{b}$, and $c(n, n) - c(n - 1, n - 1) = 2$. So (iii) applies with the bound $2G$. By Theorem \claimref{synthesis.tower-pairing-gap-at-fixed-charges-is-twice-the-quasiparticle-energy}(i), every level of the sector $(N_{a}, N_{c})$ is $K(2p + s_{a} + s_{c}) - G(j + j_{z})(j - j_{z} + 1)$ with $p$ pairs on $\Omega = n_{b} - s_{a} - s_{c}$ blocks; the last factor is largest at $j = \Omega/2$, where it is $p(\Omega - p + 1)$. So every level with $p$ pairs and $s = s_{a} + s_{c}$ singly occupied blocks is at least
\[
2Kp + Ks - Gp(n_{b} - s - p + 1) = E(p) + Ks + Gps \ge E(p), \qquad E(n) = 2Kn - Gn(n_{b} - n + 1),
\]
the band of Proposition \claimref{field-theory.composite-scalars-mean-field-level}(2), the lowest level of the sector $(n, n)$; its vector is $\psi_{n} = (P^{*})^{n}\Omega$, the quasi-spin state of Proposition \claimref{field-theory.how-close-tower-comes-ccr} with $j = n_{b}/2$, $j_{z} = n - n_{b}/2$. Hence the ground energy of $H_{4}$ on all of $\mathcal{F}$ is $\min_{n}E(n)$. Completing the square, $E(n) = Gn^{2} - (G(n_{b} + 1) - 2K)n = G(n - \gamma)^{2} - G\gamma^{2}$ with $\gamma = (n_{b} + 1)/2 - K/G$, so the minimum over integers $0 \le n \le n_{b}$ is at the integer $n^{*}$ nearest $\gamma$ (clamped to $0$ when $\gamma < \tfrac12$); since $\gamma \le (n_{b} + 1)/2 \le n_{b} - \tfrac12$ for $n_{b} \ge 2$, a minimiser $n^{*} \le n_{b} - 1$ can always be chosen; the equality $\gamma = n_{b} - \tfrac12$ occurs only at $n_{b} = 2$, $K = 0$, where $E(1) = E(2)$ is the degenerate coupling $n = 1$ of (c). The quasi-spin ladder gives $P^{*}\psi_{n} = \psi_{n+1}$, $P\psi_{n} = n(n_{b} - n + 1)\psi_{n-1}$, and $\|P^{*}\psi_{n}\|^{2} = (j - j_{z})(j + j_{z} + 1)\|\psi_{n}\|^{2} = (n + 1)(n_{b} - n)\|\psi_{n}\|^{2}$, $\|P\psi_{n}\|^{2} = (j + j_{z})(j - j_{z} + 1)\|\psi_{n}\|^{2} = n(n_{b} - n + 1)\|\psi_{n}\|^{2}$.

(a) $n^{*} \ge 1$ exactly when $\gamma > \tfrac12$, that is $Gn_{b} > 2K$ (at $Gn_{b} = 2K$, $E(0) = E(1)$). Then $E(n^{*} \pm 1) - E(n^{*}) = G((n^{*} \pm 1 - \gamma)^{2} - (n^{*} - \gamma)^{2}) = G(1 \pm 2(n^{*} - \gamma))$, and $|n^{*} - \gamma| \le \tfrac12$ puts both in $[0, 2G]$ with sum $2G$: the bound of (iii) holds with equality, as (ii) says it must, since $P^{*}\psi_{n^{*}}$ and $P\psi_{n^{*}}$ are lowest vectors of their sectors. $(P + P^{*})\psi_{n^{*}} = \psi_{n^{*}+1} + n^{*}(n_{b} - n^{*} + 1)\psi_{n^{*}-1}$, with the norms above. The pair-breaking threshold at fixed numbers is $Gn_{b}$ above the band (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.tower-pairing-gap-at-fixed-charges-is-twice-the-quasiparticle-energy}(ii)), so the larger rotor difference over the threshold is at most $2G/(Gn_{b}) = 2/n_{b}$; at the gap equation $Gn_{b} = 2E$ of (iii) there, the rotor is at most $4E/n_{b}$.

(b) If $Gn_{b} < 2K$ then $\gamma < \tfrac12$, $n^{*} = 0$, and every other level is positive: band levels $E(p) = p(2K - G(n_{b} - p + 1)) \ge p(2K - Gn_{b}) > 0$ for $p \ge 1$, and levels with $s \ge 1$ exceed $E(p) + Ks > 0$ ($K > Gn_{b}/2 > 0$). So $\Omega$ is the unique ground state, $P^{*}\Omega = \psi_{1}$ has energy $E(1) = 2K - Gn_{b} > 0$, and the sector $(1, 1)$ also contains the level $2K$ (one $a$ and one $c$ on different blocks, $p = 0$, $s_{a} = s_{c} = 1$). As $Gn_{b} \to 2K$ from below, $E(1) \to 0$.

(c) At $K/G = n_{b}/2 - n$ with $0 \le n \le \lfloor n_{b}/2\rfloor$ an integer (the range where $K \ge 0$, which the bound $E(p) + Ks + Gps \ge E(p)$ uses), $\gamma = n + \tfrac12$, so $E(n) = E(n + 1) = \min E$ and the ground eigenspace contains $\psi_{n}$ and $\psi_{n+1}$; for $\psi = \psi_{n} + \psi_{n+1}$, $\langle\psi, P\psi\rangle = \langle\psi_{n}, P\psi_{n+1}\rangle = \|P^{*}\psi_{n}\|^{2} = (n + 1)(n_{b} - n)\|\psi_{n}\|^{2} \ne 0$. The ground eigenspace is always the span of the band vectors $\psi_{n}$ with $E(n) = \min E$: a level with $s = 0$ and $j < n_{b}/2$ lies strictly above $E(p)$, since $(j + j_{z})(j - j_{z} + 1) = j(j + 1) - j_{z}(j_{z} - 1)$ increases strictly with $j$; a level with $s \ge 1$ is at least $E(p) + Ks + Gps$, which exceeds $\min E$ unless $K = 0$ and $p = 0$, and then it equals $E(0) = 0 > E(n^{*})$, because $K = 0$ gives $\gamma = (n_{b} + 1)/2 \ge \tfrac32$ and $E(n^{*}) = -Gn^{*}(n_{b} - n^{*} + 1) < 0$. So at every other coupling, where the minimiser $n^{*}$ is unique, the ground state is $\psi_{n^{*}}$ up to a factor, it lies in the sector $(n^{*}, n^{*})$, and by (i) it has $\langle P\rangle = 0$.

\emph{Reading (argued).} The uniform pair field is the helicity-zero composite scalar of the floor. Clauses (iv)(a) and (iv)(b) say exactly how its gap behaves: with a condensate ($n^{*} \ge 1$) its whole weight from the ground state sits on the two neighbouring band levels, within $2G$, and no weight at the threshold; this is the Goldstone rotor of the broken pair phase (the flat phase direction of Proposition \claimref{field-theory.composite-scalars-mean-field-level}(4) seen at finite size), and in the collective limit at fixed mean-field gap it closes as $4E/n_{b}$. Without a condensate the bound pair is gapped, at $2K - Gn_{b}$, and the gap closes where condensation begins. Clause (i) is what makes a finite order parameter need degeneracy across sectors, and (iii) is the finite form of the Goldstone theorem for a pairing-type element: it needs only $[H_{0}, X] = \varepsilon X$ and a commutator $[X, X^{*}]$ that is a function of the charges, so it covers several species paired by one uniform field with a common shell energy, and any extra term in $H_{0}$ that commutes with $X$. For a composite Higgs doublet, (i) applies to each charge the doublet carries; in a condensed doublet the directions of the broken charges are of this rotor kind, so a gapped composite doublet would have to be one that does not condense, or a mode outside the condensate's pair channel (such as a particle-number-conserving hopping doublet). The doublet floor and two-condensate couplings, where $[X, X^{*}]$ is no longer a function of the charges, are not treated here.
